newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai Worldbest expects to double profit in '96.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Worldbest expects to double profit in '96.

text.p: Chemical fibres manufacturer Shanghai Worldbest Co Ltd has a name which is difficult to live up to, but the firm's general manager said on Thursday they planned to start by doubling profits this year over last year.
The firm listed on the Shanghai stock exchange in July and was immediately the butt of jokes among stockbrokers who were sceptical of its prospects.
General manager Xiao Baoheng is determined to prove them wrong.

"We chose the name because we want to be an internationally top-rate company," Xiao said in an interview. "The Huayuan Group of which we are a part has all the elements necessary to make it possible."

The company, which listed foreign currency B shares on the Shanghai stock exchange in July, reported profits of 33.56 million yuan in 1995 and 30.66 million in the first half of 1996, but gave no figure for the first half of last year.
The company's main business is chemical fibres but it also has weaving, dyeing and garment manufacturing plants.
"For the whole year, we have a target of 80.57 million yuan net profit and there should be no trouble in reaching it," Xiao said. "We expect to double profits and next year we will do even better."
An analyst with a foreign brokerage firm said the investment community was treating Worldbest's predictions with caution.
"What they say sounds good, but we will wait and see how they fare in the actual results for the year," the analyst said.

Xiao attributed the dramatic profit growth to a combination of positive factors -- falling raw material costs, an expanding domestic market and lack of major competitors except from imports which are higher-priced because of tariffs and transport costs.
He said the company was planning various strategies to raise production in 1997 and 1998, including importation of advanced machinery and joint venture projects with foreign companies.
"We will also look at buying or merging with other companies in the same business in order to expand output. We are doing checks on one company right now," Xiao said.
The company's long-range plan, over a period of 3-5 years, is to expand chemical fibre production to 150,000-200,000 tonnes per year from 17,000 tonnes this year, he said.
On Thursday, shares in Worldbest ended at $0.284, unchanged from Wednesday.
